mechanism_narrative: Transit-station mobility is the fastest-normalizing discretionary-travel series in this snapshot, rising every week from -37.1 to -26.6. Because transit ridership and non-essential retail trips share the same trip-generation pool, the upward transit slope mechanically pulls RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -37.1 to -26.6 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT continues to rise week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility is draining steadily from 9.0 to 5.1 as households spend fewer hours at home. Once the residential weekly mean falls below 6.0, the marginal hour shifted out of the home is disproportionately converted into discretionary retail trips rather than work trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 6.0 percent-change-from-baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 9.0 to 5.1 over four weekly means
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL prints below 6.0 for two consecutive weeks and the 28-day-forward RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Outdoor activity and transit use are rising together (PARKS from -14.4 to +5.6, TRANSIT from -37.1 to -26.6). The joint movement marks a broad re-expansion of trip budgets; only when both climb simultaneously does the released travel capacity spill into indoor discretionary venues, so the effect is super-additive rather than the sum of the two series.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean positive while TRANSIT posts a week-on-week gain
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS crossed zero at t-2w and reached +5.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS is positive and TRANSIT rises, the subsequent 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is no higher than in weeks where TRANSIT rises alone.

mechanism_narrative: Under an easing-restrictions regime, the workplace series is the binding constraint on weekday retail: WORKPLACES is still -11.3 but improving every week. As office occupancy recovers, lunchtime and after-work retail footfall in commercial districts returns, so RETAIL_REC continues to climb for four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean improves by at least 1.0 point versus the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -17.0 to -11.3 over four weekly means
regime_hint: easing restrictions with office return underway
failure_condition: Under continued easing, WORKPLACES improves week-on-week yet the 28-day-forward RETAIL_REC mean fails to exceed the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The four-week window spans the late-winter daylight expansion, and PARKS already moved from -14.4 to +5.6 as outdoor conditions improve. Longer days shift leisure spending from delivery-at-home toward errand-linked trips, which structurally lifts retail-and-recreation mobility through the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises by more than 10 points versus four weeks earlier
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS gained 20.0 points between t-3w and t-0w
regime_hint: late-winter seasonal transition to longer daylight
failure_condition: PARKS records a four-week gain above 10 points while the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is flat or lower than the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility has sat flat near +9.0 for four weeks, which is the signature of a stable precautionary pantry-loading plateau. If that series breaks upward past +10.0 it signals renewed household withdrawal from discretionary outings, dragging RETAIL_REC lower within a single week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean rises above 10.0 percent-change-from-baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM held in a narrow 8.7-9.3 band across all four weekly means
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 10.0 and the following week's RETAIL_REC is unchanged or higher than the week before.

mechanism_narrative: Retail recovery in this snapshot is powered by steady commuting normalization rather than by retail itself. A persistent workplace gain of at least one point per week for two consecutive weeks is the threshold that converts commuting volume into sustained in-store browsing, so RETAIL_REC extends its climb over two more weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean gains at least 1.0 point in two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES weekly deltas were +2.6, +2.0, +1.1 across the snapshot
failure_condition: Two consecutive week-on-week WORKPLACES gains of 1.0 point or more are followed by a 28-day RETAIL_REC mean below the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of falling residential mobility and rising transit use is the cleanest read on restrictions being lifted: home-stay drops only when people leave for destinations. When RESIDENTIAL declines while TRANSIT rises in the same week, the released trips are discretionary, and RETAIL_REC accelerates over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week while TRANSIT rises week-on-week in the same observation week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 9.0 to 5.1 while TRANSIT rose -37.1 to -26.6 over the same four weeks
regime_hint: restriction easing with simultaneous decline in home-stay
failure_condition: Weeks showing a residential decline combined with a transit rise are not followed by a higher 28-day-forward RETAIL_REC mean than weeks without the joint pattern.
